metadata.title: Finite generation of the second homology group of the genus three Torelli group
metadata.abstract: We prove that the group $H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated, where $\mathcal{I}_3$ is the Torelli subgroup of the mapping class group of a closed genus-three surface $\Sigma_3$. A key role in the proof is played by establishing the following property: for each symplectic transvection $t_x\in\mathrm{Sp}_{6}(\mathbb{Z})$, we have $$ \bigl(t^{120}_x-1\bigr)^{57}\bigl(t_x^{24}-1\bigr)(t_x-1)^6H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})=0. $$ The proof is based on the study of the spectral sequences associated with the action of $\mathcal{I}_3$ on the Bestvina-Bux-Margalit complex of minimizing cycles and with the actions on certain auxiliary complexes of the stabilizers of two- and three-component multicurves on $\Sigma_3$. The remaining ingredients are Tavgen's theorem, which asserts that $\mathrm{Sp}_{6}(\mathbb{Z})$ has bounded elementary generation, and the result of Kassabov and Putman, which asserts that $H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated as a $\mathbb{Z}[\mathrm{Sp}_6(\mathbb{Z})]$-module.
